SuperValu removes frozen and chilled food from shelves at 13 stores after cyberattack on fridges
The Irish Times, November 2, 2026

SuperValu experienced a cyberattack on refrigeration systems affecting 13 stores, forcing removal of chilled and frozen products as a precaution. By Monday afternoon, the company stated the issue was "fully resolved," with replenishment efforts underway.
Affected stores included locations in Lucan, Blanchardstown, Waterford, and Bray. Expected losses in thousands of euros. Only specific refrigerator models were compromised. Other products remained unaffected and stores stayed open.

"Our monitoring systems alerted us to the issue, and we took immediate action," a Musgrave Group spokesman said, adding that "customer safety is our first priority."

The incident follows similar attacks across Europe. Swedish and Belgian supermarkets experienced freezers overheated to 55 degrees, while French retailers suffered attacks last month affecting 700 stores, including Intermarché and Carrefour locations.

Utz Roedig, University College Cork computer science professor, noted the attacker's likely motivation was "disruption to our everyday life" rather than direct financial gain, suggesting either an individual or potentially state-sponsored activity.
The French attacks exploited internet-connected fridge controllers, allowing remote manipulation of temperature settings to trigger defrost cycles.
